title: Table Storage
description: Store semi-structured NoSQL data in Azure Table Storage using simple key-value and property-based patterns.

data.text: Azure Table Storage is a NoSQL key-value store for semi-structured data. It is simple, fast, and very cheap. Each **table** holds **entities**, and each entity has a **partition key** and **row key** that together form a unique ID. Beyond those two keys, you can store up to 255 custom properties per entity.

data.title: Good Fit
items: **Telemetry and logs** — append-only or semi-structured device or application data.
**User profiles** — flexible attributes that vary per user without schema migrations.
**Address books and catalogs** — simple lookups by user or product ID.
**Prototyping** — quickly persist data without designing a relational schema.

data.text: The **partition key** groups related entities together for scalability and query performance. The **row key** uniquely identifies an entity within a partition. Together they form the primary key. Choose a partition key that distributes traffic evenly across partitions.

terms.definition: A collection of entities in Table Storage, similar to a database table but schema-less.
A single item in a table, identified by partition key and row key, with up to 255 custom properties.
The first part of an entity's primary key used to group entities for scalability.
The second part of the primary key that uniquely identifies an entity within its partition.

data.title: Table Storage vs Cosmos DB Table API
data.text: Table Storage is the original, low-cost option. Cosmos DB Table API provides global distribution, dedicated throughput, and lower latency at a higher price. Choose based on your scale and consistency needs.

data.title: Exercise: Store and Query User Data
data.description: Create a table, insert entities, and query them by partition.
steps: Create a storage account and a table named 'Tasks'.
Insert three task entities with different partition keys (e.g., 'proj-a', 'proj-b').
Query all entities in partition 'proj-a' using C# or Azure CLI.
Insert a second entity with the same row key but different partition and observe that both coexist.
data.expectedOutcome: A working table with entities that can be queried by partition.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Table Storage is a simple, low-cost NoSQL key-value store.
Entities are identified by partition key and row key.
Schemas are flexible: each entity can have different properties.
Choose partition keys that spread load evenly across partitions.
data.takeaway: Table Storage is ideal for semi-structured data that does not need relational features.
